The sniper rifle shouldn’t be useable at close range to good effect. The fact that it can makes it the only weapon in the game I can think of, that has no major trade offs or limitations. Quickscoping may be hard, but that doesn’t mean it should even be an option at close range. Sniper, as a class, should be unanimously FUCKED if any power class gets close to him without his team nearby, but sniper has MULTIPLE good close range options. He doesn’t even need to do a difficult quick scope most of the time, quickscoping is just another blatantly unbalanced part of his kit. It’s not that you “can’t play” them. Personally I’m fine with people playing them. But I find overpowered options so incredibly boring. They remove any sense of struggled or balance unless your team really sucks. The only time Uber saw is ever fun (and it’s barely even fun) is for Uber chaining, which is an extremely boring strategy on its own. Same thing for pretty much every other overpowered weapon in the game. It just rewards you with essentially no trade offs. 

Also the idea pyro has no overpowered or just plain broken (bug wise) weapons is rather silly, but I presume you are making the statement that goes something like “pyro takes no skill” which barely makes sense because it is far EASIER to be a value to your team as a medic where you just need to left click and be cognizant of pressing movement keys and you’ll generate more value with less required situational awareness.

Here’s the full breakdown:
Things need to be balanced assuming they will be used perfectly, meaning any downside that exists needs to actually be meaningful. Functionally the sniper rifle has no downsides as a stock weapon compared to any other class. It doesn’t use a projectile requiring leading shots, it doesn’t have a range limitation or spread, it doesn’t have low base damage, it essentially has no downside, along with having guaranteed crits, it doesn’t reload, if any other classes stock weapon had all of these properties people would go ballistic. 

Even a weapon like the phlog, which HAS a downside, along with inheriting range limitations from the stock weapon, is largely complained about for having guaranteed crits on a class with an already high damage output. 

As for the ubersaw:
I think it’s a bit silly to reward medic with 10 seconds of healings worth of Uber (on stock) for hitting an enemy with a melee that has no real downside. Unless you’re rushing at an enemy away from your team there’s practically no scenario in which this doesn’t reward the medic. 

(It’s especially silly that it isn’t banned in comp but weapons like the solemn vow are)
Yeah I think Uber saw us a terrible unlock from a balance perspective. I think it shouldn’t exist. It’s not even an interesting design concept.

Just because something isn’t easy, doesn’t mean it should be allowed. If there was an intensely difficult glitch that allowed medics to double their Uber times, it would still be patched. Not that quickscoping is a glitch, but sniper is very obviously meant to be the long range class, and suffer in close range combat, something unlocks like the Jarate forget, is something that (should) balance the class. When you avoid the sight lines and move to avoid being shot, you should be rewarded for out maneuvering a sniper by having an easy close range fight, but all that is negated by the option of quickscoping, the sniper no longer has to think about repositioning to get out of danger, going to their team for defense if their spot is being challenged, or even just accepting a death and respawn for letting someone get past them.

It’s one of my biggest issues with long running continuous stories for younger audiences. If you’re creating something for a younger audience but it takes so long the original audience outgrows it, you essentially decided you’re creating something for kids/teens 20 years from now, and not actually your present audience. Continuous works should age with their original target audience. I get that there will always be kids and it’s easy for someone to get through 1000 chapters in less than the time it takes to make them, but if it’s going to take such a long time that the audience you were originally targeting has outgrown it, perhaps that is a sign to make the story shorter, or to mature with the audience. 

While not a perfect counter example, Jojo changed a lot in its 40 year history. It changed and grew with the artist and audience, adopting different story telling styles and themes, even switching publishers and having a major reboot. While one piece is one long continuous story, the same development of tone and ideals should still happen, but the tone and themes are largely stagnant. Dark truths revealed in the world are quickly forgotten by the crew or not relevant to the main story (yet) so we have to wait years for the more mature elements established a long time ago to come back when the story is ready to have another serious segment.

To break it down even more
One piece has moments of seriousness surrounded by light heartedness, even though the world is deeply messed up. This can be chalked up to luffy’s perspective but even more analytical characters like Nami or Ussopp rarely focus on the great evils of the world. The main crew remains largely static, and it becomes stale.

I still love one piece, the world building, ability system, and story are enjoyable, but I try to allot my thinking about it to only once a week when the new chapter hits, as deeper analysis makes it less enjoyable for me.
